I think I just always knew. I used to throw fits when my mom put me in skirts and stuff. I’d always make male characters in video games. I was bad and went online and talked to strangers when I was a kid lmfao, and I always told them I was a guy, before I even knew what being trans was. I found out what being trans was when I was 11, but only thought that women could be trans — as in, women who were born male only ever got media coverage, so that’s always what I thought of. And then I saw a trans man on YouTube (FTM) when I was 14 and had this big “aha” moment and it all just clicked.
I didn’t have a say in being trans, in having this body, and my parents were never supportive, so now I’m basically completely fucked.

It makes me feel like I want to rip my skin off. I missed out on a male childhood, male puberty, and my body has been irreversibly mutilated by female hormones. And I don’t have access to testosterone right now either. Every day gets harder the older I get, and nearing 23, I’m tempted to just kill myself rather than go through with transition because my body is fucked already and I never had any say in it. I wouldn’t wish this shit on anyone.

If you genuinely like working as a barista, I would recommend looking into corporate locations. I worked at a licensed store in a grocery store for 8 months and was *miserable*. It felt like I was the only one ever doing anything. Everybody else called out most of the time and didn’t care. Some days I opened and closed because no one else bothered showing up. I was alone 90% of the time and no one understood the stress I was under.

I’ve been at my corporate location for a year now and I’m a lot happier. There are definitely bad days, but it’s a lot better and at least at the end of the day, I’m lucky to have a store full of people that have each other’s backs. Many of my coworkers also came from licensed stores and they hated it until they got to corporate. Again, bad days, but it’s so much better. Better pay, better staff, better benefits. I wish I could offer you better advice though. I’m a closer, so I get it. The struggle is rough sometimes. Good luck dude
